services.name: Written attic check
services.blurb: Depth measured in six spots, leaks photographed, and a written report before any price.

services.name: Blown-in attic top-up
services.blurb: Loose-fill added to the depth on your report, with depth rulers left in the attic.

services.name: Attic air sealing
services.blurb: Top plates, wire holes and light boxes sealed with foam and caulk, each one photographed.

services.name: Rim joist spray foam
services.blurb: Foam along the basement band joist, the spot prairie wind finds first in most ranches.

services.name: Bonus room over the garage
services.blurb: Cold floors and walls of rooms above garages opened, sealed and filled to the right depth.

services.name: Old vermiculite: test first
services.blurb: If we see pebble-like fill, we stop, explain the lab test and leave it undisturbed.

services.name: Split-level and ranch walls
services.blurb: Hollow walls of 1950s to 1970s houses filled with dense-pack cellulose through small holes.

services.name: Bath fan venting
services.blurb: Bath fans that dump into the attic rerouted outside, so moisture stops frosting the roof boards.

proof.label: Sample

reviews.text: The report had a depth for each part of the attic. Over our bedroom it was three and a half inches, by the hatch almost nothing. The price matched the report line by line.
reviews.name: Dale P.

reviews.text: The room over our garage was 58 degrees all January. They found gaps at the floor edge and almost no insulation where it meets the outside wall. Now it holds the same as the rest of the house.
reviews.name: Nicole V.

reviews.text: They saw the shiny pebbles in our attic and stopped right there. No pressure, just how the lab test works and what our choices were. We had it tested before anything else happened.
reviews.name: Gary O.

reviews.text: Wind used to whistle at the top of the basement walls. The foam on the rim joist took one day and the basement family room is finally usable in winter.
reviews.name: Lisa M.

reviews.text: I liked the rulers stapled to the rafters. When our buyer's inspector went up, he read the depth off them and wrote it in his report. Easy.
reviews.name: Brent A.

reviews.text: Our split-level had hollow walls on the windy side. They drilled small holes, filled them and plugged them. Hard to spot from the driveway, and the north bedroom stopped being the cold one.
reviews.name: Anita R.

proof.guarantee: Your report lists the depth we promise. If a ruler reads less within a year, we top it up at our cost.

prices.note: to the typical R-49 to R-60 range
